judged_text: In sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but this call site does `const token = res?.data` (a Response has no data property and res.json() is never called on the sync response) and then dereferences token.access_token. With sharing enabled, every Google calendar refresh dereferences undefined (`token.access_token`) and throws inside the try block, so the sync endpoint's valid tokens are never read and all Google calendar operations for synced users fail.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when sharing is enabled it returns the raw `fetch(...)` result (a `Response`). In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the caller assumes the return value has a `.data` property (`const token = res?.data;`) and then dereferences `token.access_token` / `token.expiry_date`. A `Response` has no `.data` and the code never calls `await res.json()` for the sharing-path response, so `token` will be `undefined` and the refresh path will throw for synced users.
